extracted.intended_audience: managers, executives-in-training, researchers, and other professionals writing proposals or technical reports (including grant and project proposals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklist for composing persuasive, well-structured proposals and reports (research or business) using a self-monitoring negative checklist to spot and correct errors during development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-Monitoring Negative Checklist (SMNC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presented as a series of thirty-one warnings of what can go wrong in a proposal; a mode of outlining that provokes the writer to think more critically and self-defensively and to account for the reader's objections long before the reader makes them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduces cognitive dissonance or calculated frustration; assumes error so writer admits and corrects errors early; used as an on-going correction mechanism, systematic and continuously monitoring proposal development; can be used for reverse engineering breakdowns to focus on missing goals and to resolve conflicts, anomalies, gaps, and questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research problem not clearly stated / poorly located / not well-understood
rubrics_metrics.description: --research problem not clearly stated, poorly located, not well-understood
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard against choosing a 'non-problem' or confusing symptoms with the real problem; properly factor the problem and locate its cause, nature, and effects; set the problem in context of prior work so reader sees need for study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implications of problem not presented or unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: --implications of problem not presented or unclear
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly present the implications so the reader understands why the problem matters and what consequences follow if it is not addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem too narrow
rubrics_metrics.description: --problem too narrow
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid an excessively constrained problem focus that yields trivial or uninteresting results; ensure scope is sufficient to merit study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem too broad / unmanageable / not factored
rubrics_metrics.description: --problem too broad, unmanageable focus, not outlined for study, not properly factored into its parts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor the problem into manageable parts, outline the study focus, and ensure the proposal's scope is practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: No understanding of the problem's environment or context
rubrics_metrics.description: --no understanding of the problem's environment or context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate the problem to the field; demonstrate awareness of how prior studies and the environment shape the problem framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem situation not reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: --problem situation not reviewed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a review or background that locates the problem historically and situationally for the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: No separation of problem, causes, nature, effects
rubrics_metrics.description: --no separation of problem, causes, nature, effects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly separate and label the problem itself from its causes and effects to avoid confusion about what is being studied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature search thin / unrepresentative / poorly sampled
rubrics_metrics.description: --literature search thin, unrepresentative range, poorly sampled
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct a comprehensive, representative literature search to situate the study and show command of the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research resources unbalanced or poor quality
rubrics_metrics.description: --research resources unbalanced, poor quality, unrepresentative of the field, do not demonstrate knowledge of available research tools
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use balanced, high-quality resources that demonstrate knowledge of available tools and methods in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confusion of primary/secondary or qualitative/quantitative/data types
rubrics_metrics.description: --confusion of primary and secondary, qualitative and quantitative, or structured and unstructured data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly distinguish data types and their roles; match data collection to the study's needs and avoid conflating categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate or poorly constructed instruments/models/statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: --survey instrument, model, or statistics gathering techniques inappropriate to need, poorly constructed, biased, incomplete, unscientific, does not demonstrate knowledge of the field, does not demonstrate ability to design a survey instrument, run an experiment, or apply a model
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure instruments, models, and statistical techniques are appropriate, well-designed, unbiased, and demonstrate competence in their use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data inappropriate to conclusions / poor quality or quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: --data inappropriate to conclusions drawn, data poor in quality or quantity, secondary, unreliable, immaterial, unverifiable, unobjective
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect data that legitimately support the conclusions; prioritize primary, verifiable, and relevant data of sufficient quantity and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology poorly chosen / insufficient / unexplained
rubrics_metrics.description: --methodology poorly chosen, insufficient, inappropriate, poorly designed, unobjective, unexplained
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a methodology that matches the problem and objectives, explain it clearly, and design it to be objective and sufficient to answer the research questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confusion of facts, opinions, assumptions, and/or hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: --confusion of facts, opinions, assumptions, and/or hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep factual findings, opinions, assumptions, and hypotheses distinct in presentation and analysis to avoid misleading argumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis weak / not data-grounded / unsystematic
rubrics_metrics.description: --analysis weak, not grounded in data, unsystematic, unstructured, unable to correlate results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use systematic, data-grounded analysis capable of correlating results and demonstrating how findings arise from data.

rubrics_metrics.name: No sense of the whole or interrelationship of parts
rubrics_metrics.description: --no sense of the whole, its constituent parts, or the interrelationship of those parts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a clear conception of the whole study and how individual parts relate to one another; avoid isolated or disconnected sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptualization weak / theoretically incomplete
rubrics_metrics.description: --conceptualization weak, theoretically incomplete, not understood in application
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a sound conceptual/theoretical framework and show how it is applied in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument not apparent / poorly connected / unconvincing
rubrics_metrics.description: --argument not apparent, poorly handled, incompletely connected, unconvincing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a clear, logically connected argument from problem through method to conclusions that persuades the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-solving approach not defined or purposive
rubrics_metrics.description: --problem-solving approach not carefully defined or sufficiently purposive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the problem-solving approach explicitly and ensure it is purposive and aligned with objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical fallacies / weak intellectual grasp
rubrics_metrics.description: --logical fallacies, weak intellectual grasp of the problem
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid logical fallacies; demonstrate intellectual mastery of the problem domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives not explicitly stated or concrete
rubrics_metrics.description: --not explicitly stated or concrete
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State objectives clearly and concretely; do not leave them vague or abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives not established by priority
rubrics_metrics.description: --not established by priority
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize objectives so the reader knows which aims are primary and which are secondary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives confused with problem, solution, or procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: --confused with problem, solution, or procedures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate objectives from the problem statement, proposed solutions, and procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives lacking criteria for measuring success
rubrics_metrics.description: --lacking criteria for measuring successful achievement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific, measurable criteria by which successful achievement of objectives can be judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical applications / recommendations not provided
rubrics_metrics.description: --practical applications, future possibilities, or recommendations not provided
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State practical applications, future possibilities, and recommendations that flow from achieving the objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need to address the problem not identified or validated
rubrics_metrics.description: --need to address the problem not identified or validated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate and validate the need for the study using authoritative testimony, statistics, or other evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and implications of the study not demonstrated
rubrics_metrics.description: --relevance and implication of study not demonstrated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the study's relevance to its field and its broader implications for related problem areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research purpose unclear or inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: --research purpose unclear, inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify and justify the study's purpose and ensure it is appropriate to the problem and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research design poorly conceived / incomplete blueprint
rubrics_metrics.description: --research design poorly conceived, not carefully tied together, incomplete blueprint for study
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a coherent, detailed research design that serves as a complete blueprint for conducting the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research design idealistic but not concretely structured
rubrics_metrics.description: --research design ideal, not concretely structured, poor guiding mechanism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly idealized designs; ensure the design is concretely structured and will guide actual implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended proposal structure and sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Example outline: Summary; I. Introduction (Explanation, Background, Prior Studies); Choice of Material for Study; Methodology; III. Particular Problems Posed; IV. Organization of the Project (Division of Time, Division of Responsibilities, Schedule for Completion, Use of Funds); V. Results of the Project; VI. Significance of the Task; VII. Qualifications of Participants; VIII. Bibliography or Materials List.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this skeletal structure (or similar) to ensure relevant parts are included, properly proportioned, not overlapping, and clearly related to the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label abstract sections clearly (Problem / Purpose / Results)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective labelling would have aided the reader in the body of the abstract through such simple sub-headings as Problem, Purpose, Results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear subheadings to avoid confusing problems, methods, goals, benefits, and implications; consider preparing a skeletal design before drafting the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match method to problem and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever method is chosen must appropriately match the problem and objectives of the study (e.g., survey methodology for data generation; developmental for formulating a program; implementative for enacting a product; validating for testing a product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design procedures appropriate to the chosen method: experimental designs need variables, targeted subjects, control groups, and analysis methods; survey designs require instrument description, conduct, sample, and correlation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer three immediate methodological questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask: what data is requisite to answer the questions; where is that data to be found; what is the most effective means of gathering and analyzing that data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answering these within the SMNC boundaries will resolve the researcher's choice of methodology and ensure methodological fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating the proposal: persuade reader to support the solution
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective in writing is not to solve a problem, but to persuade the reader to support the solving of that problem; must pique curiosity, convince the reader to repose confidence in the writer, and lead the reader to feel he is participating in the formulation or solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four techniques: introduce the problem first; maintain objectivity and be information-oriented; stress benefits of solving the problem; keep the proposal sufficiently open-ended so the mechanism is detailed but the solution is posed as a hypothesis rather than 'giving away' results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal must establish credibility and deliver what is promised
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal will sell itself if it has established the researcher's credibility and the validity of his technical demonstration; if it delivers what is promised and demonstrates an understanding of the implications and applications of what has been delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure credibility (qualifications, competence), realistic promises, and clear demonstration of how results will be applied and what implications arise.
